items.title: Advantages and Disadvantages of Network Topologies

source_refs.note: Sub-heading 'Advantages and Disadvantages of Network Topologies' of 1.5 as printed (PDF 11-12, printed 6-7).

blocks.text: Different topologies offer different benefits. Some are easy to install and low-cost (as shown in Table 1.1). Others provide high reliability and performance. Certain topologies are easy to expand. Some are difficult to manage and expensive. Choosing the right topology depends on network needs.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Some topologies are simple and cheap. Others are reliable but costly. Some are easy to expand. Others are difficult to manage. Choice depends on needs.

blocks.caption: Table 1.1: Advantages & Disadvantages of Network Topologies
rows:
• Simple and easy to install
• Requires less cable
• Cost-effective

• Failure of main cable affects whole network
• Difficult to troubleshoot
• Performance decreases with more devices

• Easy to install and manage
• Failure of one device does not affect others
• Easy to detect faults

• Central device failure stops entire network
• Requires more cable
• Higher cost

• Data flows in an organized manner
• No data collision
• Equal access for all devices

• Failure of one device affects whole network
• Difficult to add/remove devices
• Rarely used today

• Highly reliable and fault-tolerant
• Multiple paths for data
• High security

• Very expensive
• Complex installation
• Requires large number of cables

• Easy to expand
• Suitable for large networks
• Hierarchical management

• Backbone failure affects whole network
• Complex setup
• More cabling required
